title: Paper order state and startup reconcile — design resolved into testable contracts, no orders
verdict_note: both Stage 5T open questions are resolved into pure, tested contracts (24 tests, no broker, no socket). Two prerequisites are named; neither is an ambiguity, both are work

why_the_ledger_cannot_own_it.evidence: window_ledger._write catches every exception and disables the channel for the process; its comment says 'It must never escape into a trading path — the ledger records availability, it does not enforce it'
why_the_ledger_cannot_own_it.conclusion: exactly right for evidence, exactly wrong for a write-ahead log: a failed write would let an order go out with no record of intent
why_the_ledger_cannot_own_it.pinned_by_test: a test parses _write and requires it still swallows, so a change to that contract forces a re-read of this decision

three_files_three_contracts.on_write_failure: ABORT the order before it is sent
advances only on a CONFIRMED fill

states.intended: written BEFORE any broker call; the book admitted it, nothing sent
states.submitted: handed to the broker; outcome not known and must not be assumed
states.rejected: the broker definitively refused; nothing is held
states.unknown: the broker did not answer, or answered unusably

A_order_state.rejected_is_not_unknown: 'no' and 'I could not hear you' are different facts; treating the second as the first is how a filled order becomes a position nobody believes in
A_order_state.the_core_guarantee: INTENDED -> FILLED is NOT a legal transition; intent can never be mistaken for a fill because the journal will not accept the history
A_order_state.impossible_history_handling: reported, never smoothed — a reader that quietly repairs the journal is a reader that can be lied to

decided_field_unchanged.must_not_depend_on_a_fill: a broker outage would read as the strategy having stopped deciding, and shadow and paper evidence would stop being comparable — the premise the Stage 5S readiness gate rests on
decided_field_unchanged.pinned_by_test: classify_slot_row is parsed and must mention no order word
decided_field_unchanged.shadow_behaviour: bit-identical under this design; nothing in the ledger changes

intended.restart: the candidate did not trade; book unchanged; continue once reconcile says MATCH

submitted.restart: ask the broker — get_order_status if an id was recorded, else compare positions. BLOCK entries, allow exits

partial.restart: book records the FILLED quantity only, never the requested one; remainder flagged; entries blocked

filled.restart: the book advances — the only state that may add a position

rejected.restart: the reserved cap is released and the refusal is recorded as a divergence from the shadow book

crash_recovery.close_filled_open_failed: track1_switch emits OPEN_FAILED_FLAT and calls persist_flat. If that raised, persisted=False and the book still claims the old position while the account is flat. On restart that is a MISMATCH and the repair is to believe the BROKER about existence

B_startup_reconcile.why_three_answers: IBKRBroker.get_positions() reads until two consecutive reads agree and, if they never do, WARNS and returns the last one — the caller cannot tell a settled truth from a guess. Third time in this project a status reader has had no way to say 'I do not know'; the first (scheduler_processes() -> []) cost six entry slots

verdicts.mismatch: a definite disagreement, or a journal history that cannot have happened
verdicts.unknown: positions never settled, or an order is still SUBMITTED / UNKNOWN

B_startup_reconcile.why_exits_always_allowed: refusing to REDUCE exposure while the book is confused is the wrong failure direction — a stop that cannot be placed is worse than one placed against a position that turns out to be flat
B_startup_reconcile.does_not_compare: cluster — get_positions sets it to 'UNKNOWN' because IBKR has no cluster concept, so comparing it would mismatch every time
B_startup_reconcile.netting: signed per contract, the convention ib.positions() already uses, so a LONG 1 against a SHORT 1 cannot read as agreement
B_startup_reconcile.unrecognised_instrument: blocks. The real case is a leftover full-size NKD position: _to_runner deliberately no longer maps NKD back to MNKD, so it arrives under a name the book does not use and must NOT be quietly adopted as MNKD

b1_constraint.statement: while one IB Gateway login serves both routes, get_positions() returns the net per contract for BOTH; the strongest available check is broker_net == track1_net + legacy_net

the_hole_now_asserted.reality: Track 1 holds LONG 1, legacy holds LONG 1 -> broker nets LONG 2
the_hole_now_asserted.belief: Track 1's book claims LONG 2, legacy's claims LONG 0
the_hole_now_asserted.result: MATCH, entries ALLOWED, while Track 1's book is wrong by a whole contract
the_hole_now_asserted.with_a_dedicated_account: the same broker truth is caught immediately and entries are blocked

b1_constraint.correction_made: the first version of that test asserted the opposite and passed, because the case it built (legacy claiming a SHORT it does not hold) is one that IS caught. It now asserts the hole
b1_constraint.implication: B1 is not merely a decision to record before paper — it decides whether reconcile can attribute a mismatch at all

missing_and_needed.why: no way to ask what of mine is still working; without it a SUBMITTED with no answer can only be resolved via get_order_status(order_id), which needs an id the journal can only have if the broker already returned one — the exact gap a crash lands in
to distinguish 'it never filled' from 'it filled and I missed the confirmation' without inferring it from positions

broker_methods.interim_answer: the journal writes SUBMITTED with a client-side idempotency key generated BEFORE the call, and reconcile resolves by comparing positions (existence) rather than by order id. It works, and it is weaker than it should be

legacy_b3_b4_reuse.why: both are written against live_positions.json — the first entry in run_live_day_track1.LEGACY_PATHS, the list of files this route must never write. Reusing them reintroduces the state assumptions the route was built to leave behind
legacy_b3_b4_reuse.what_is_reusable: a rule rather than code — get_positions' own docstring says B3 compares only inst/direction/contracts, and that is what reconcile implements
legacy_b3_b4_reuse.minimal_track1_reconcile: the function written this stage: ~60 lines, pure, no broker, three lists in, tri-state verdict out

pure_and_tested: OrderRecord (flat and scalar — it is read back after a crash)
resolve_journal -> final states + impossible histories, reported not repaired
reconcile(book, broker, *, broker_settled, journal, legacy_book, shared_account)
CRASH_RECOVERY (one entry per state, walked by a test)
still_unimplemented: the order journal writer, with its fail-closed contract
get_open_orders() and an executions lookup on the broker
the call site: reconcile before the first slot of a session, then per-slot order handling
tests_required_before_the_executor: the journal is fail-closed: a write that raises aborts the order before it is sent
an order is never sent without an INTENDED line already durable on disk
SUBMITTED with no answer -> reconcile UNKNOWN -> entries blocked, exits allowed
partial fill books the filled quantity only and flags the remainder
rejected fill releases the reserved cap and records a divergence
disconnect mid-order leaves a state the next process can reconcile
close-then-open's three branches, including persist_flat raising
no order when explanation, freshness or admission refused — each asserted alone
an armed run and a shadow run over the same window produce the same decisions

direct_answers.ledger_order_state_machine: six states in a separate fail-closed journal; INTENDED -> FILLED is not a legal transition; the window ledger is untouched and `decided` keeps meaning 'the route reached a decision'
direct_answers.crash_recovery: nothing sent on INTENDED; ask the broker on SUBMITTED and UNKNOWN; book the filled part only on PARTIAL; believe the broker about existence after a failed switch
direct_answers.startup_reconcile_contract: three answers; compares instrument/direction/contracts as a signed net; unrecognised instruments block; unsettled reads are UNKNOWN, not flat
direct_answers.blocks_entries_vs_allows_exits: MISMATCH and UNKNOWN both block entries; exits are allowed in all three verdicts
direct_answers.pure_vs_unimplemented: the state machine and the reconcile rule are built and tested; the journal writer, the executor, two broker methods and the call sites are not
direct_answers.accidental_order_path_today: none — four gates hold, run_shadow still builds NoOrderBroker, the scheduler's slot path takes no order gate, and neither new module is imported by anything in production
